acme_poc_admin: Hi team — running a 2-week POC for Redwood Private in eu-west-1. Architecture: customer TGW hub -> transit VPC (where our TLS MITM/firewall sits) -> Redwood connectivity. Must: 1) preserve original client src IP in logs, 2) stable egress IP per region (we can BYOIP or assign an EIP), 3) no data leaving eu-west-1. Qs: can PrivateLink deliver src IP preservation? If not, tradeoffs vs VPC peering? Any pricing delta if we run a transit reverse-proxy vs direct PrivateLink? Any enterprise blockers we should expect?

rachel_sales: Looping Tom (solutions) and Kris (neteng). Also please paste your transit VPC CIDR and rough RPS so we can size.

acme_poc_admin: CIDR 10.100.0.0/16, expected peak ~40 rps, avg ~8 rps. We prefer minimal network changes on our side.

tom_se: TL;DR: PrivateLink gives strong isolation and is easiest for allowlisting, but it terminates at our ENI so the Redwood backend sees the ENI src, not your original client IP. VPC peering (or shared subnets) can preserve client src IP end-to-end.

tom_se: Options I recommend (in order):
1) Transit reverse-proxy (in your transit VPC) with a static EIP, forward X-Forwarded-For to Redwood via PrivateLink. This gives auditability + static egress + isolates traffic.
2) VPC peering / shared VPC attachment to Redwood service — preserves src IP natively but requires route propagation & potential security review.
3) Proxyless: run traffic via peering and skip the proxy, but only if you can accept direct routing and the slightly larger blast radius.

k_ross_neteng: Practical notes from neteng: PrivateLink endpoint = AWS interface ENI in your VPC; flow logs will show ENI as source. If you require original srcip at our app logs, you must forward an application header (X-Forwarded-For) or choose peering.

k_ross_neteng: Firewall allowlist snippet for your egress NAT EIP (replace 52.50.77.88 with final EIP we give you):
```
# outbound rule to Redwood POC endpoints (eu-west-1)
dst: 52.50.77.88/32
port: 443
proto: TCP
# SNI allowlist values: private-api.redwood.internal, private.redwood-inference.com
```

sec_ops: Security checklist highlights: Integration questionnaire, network diagram showing where TLS is terminated/reissued, and a list of cert principals Redwood will see (post TLS-inspect). If you forward X-Forwarded-For, ensure you have tamper-protection (we can mutually HMAC a header if needed). Also confirm whether you need HSM-backed KMS for key storage.

acme_poc_admin: Good point on header tamper — we'll need the HMAC option. Also, is there a significant ops cost difference between running the proxy (self-hosted) vs us doing peering?

tom_se: Cost/ops delta: self-hosted transit proxy = infra + management on your side (NAT gateway / small autoscaling group). For POC sizing we estimate ~€80-120/day in variable infra (EIPs, NAT costs) plus a one-time onboarding/setup of ~€500 if Redwood assists. VPC peering path is cheaper infra-wise but adds config time and an enterprise security review that can add ~3 business days. PrivateLink-only (no proxy) reduces your infra cost but loses native srcip. I'll follow up with a short price table in the kickoff doc.

acme_poc_admin: Timeline ask: we want to start Monday. Can you provide final IPs and a 1-page diagram by Friday EOD?

k_ross_neteng: We can publish a short allowlist + diagram by Friday if the POC org approves. Example curl check you can run once EIP is assigned: 
```
curl -vk --resolve private-api.redwood.internal:443:52.50.77.88 https://private-api.redwood.internal/health
```

k_ross_neteng: That verifies SNI/DNS -> EIP binding and TLS handshake. If you use the proxy+PrivateLink flow, make sure your proxy sets X-Forwarded-For and the connection towards the PrivateLink endpoint uses the private DNS entry we provide.

deploy-bot: created ticket POC-4722 assigned to k_ross_neteng. Preflight runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc-net-preflight (access gated).

acme_poc_admin: Thanks — we'll provision the transit proxy and EIP. Please include exact CIDR exceptions and any TGW attachment steps in the diagram.

tom_se: Will do. Booking a 30-min kickoff Fri 09:30 to go over the diagram and pricing. :calendar: If we get your go/no-go by Fri AM we can meet your Monday start.

sec_ops: Also attaching a short checklist in the kickoff doc for compliance: IA, cert principals, KMS reqs, and log retention window.

acme_poc_admin: Great, appreciate it. We'll post our compliance contact and route table owners here shortly.
